title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 29 October 2026 (week 44) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report was published on 29 October 2026 (week 44), and the data is based on information up to and including week 43 of 2026 (19 October and 25 October 2026).
analysis.location_and_population: The report covers England, focusing on the population aged 75 years and over, as well as those under 75 years with a weakened immune system.
analysis.event: The report details the surveillance findings for SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), influenza, and RSV in England during week 43 of 2026. It includes data on ED attendances, confirmed ARI incidents, and influenza vaccine uptake.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: As of 27 October 2026, there were 1,847 COVID-19 cases identified in hospital settings in week 43, a decrease from 2,151 cases in the previous week. The SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity rate in hospital settings decreased slightly to 8.3% compared with 8.8% for the same period on the previous Sunday. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 11.1%, down from 13.0% in the same age group the previous week.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report is based on data up to week 43 and includes information on the unified sample dataset (USD) for SARS-CoV-2 test results. It notes that testing policy and practice may change over time, which can impact positivity rates, and that comparisons over time should be interpreted with caution. The data quality report outlines notable changes in testing policy during 2022 to 2023.

analysis.brief_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 29 October 2026 (week 44) provides an overview of the health situation in England. The report highlights that as of 27 October 2026, there were 1,847 confirmed COVID-19 cases in hospital settings during week 43, a decrease from 2,151 in the previous week. The SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity rate in hospital settings dropped slightly to 8.3% compared with 8.8% the previous week. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over, with a rolling 7-day rate of 11.1%, down from 13.0% the prior week. The report also notes that testing policy changes may affect positivity rates, and that comparisons over time should be interpreted cautiously. Additionally, it mentions that influenza activity remained stable, while RSV activity increased. The data is based on the unified sample dataset (USD) and includes information on vaccine uptake, with lower rates observed among certain age groups and higher rates among pregnant women. The report was published on 29 October 2026 and is available at the provided URL.
analysis.summary_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 29 October 2026 (week 44) provides an overview of the health situation in England. The report highlights that as of 27 October 2026, there were 1,847 confirmed COVID-19 cases in hospital settings during week 43, a decrease from 2,151 in the previous week. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over, with a rolling 7-day rate of 11.1%, down from 13.0% the prior week. analysis.time: From 31 December 2019 to 21 March 2020, and since 22 March 2020, with weekly updates from July 2023 onwards (N14, N15, N21).
analysis.location_and_population: Global, with data collected from countries, territories, and areas, including high, low, lower middle, and upper middle income groups (N1, N16).
analysis.event: WHO monitors and reports on the global epidemiological situation of SARS-CoV-2 through the WHO COVID-19 dashboard, including confirmed cases and deaths (N1, N4, N10).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The dashboard includes confirmed cases and deaths reported to WHO, with data subject to verification and potential changes due to retrospective updates or changes in reporting practices (N1, N8, N18).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO collects and disseminates data as reported by its Member States, with potential for significant data errors and corrections, and acknowledges differences in case detection, testing strategies, and reporting practices across regions (N13, N9, N18).

analysis.brief_en: The WHO COVID-19 dashboard provides a global summary of confirmed SARS-CoV-2 cases and deaths, with data collected from countries, territories, and areas. It includes information on case definitions, testing strategies, and reporting practices, which vary by region. The dashboard has been updated since March 2020, with weekly data from July 2023 onwards. Data is subject to continuous verification and may change due to retrospective updates or shifts in reporting standards. WHO acknowledges that case detection, testing, and reporting practices differ globally, which can lead to under or overestimation of true case and death counts. Additionally, some countries have stopped reporting or changed their reporting frequency, which may affect the completeness of the data. The dashboard serves as a tool for monitoring the pandemic's spread and impact, but it is important to note that the data reflects official reports and may not capture all cases or deaths accurately.
